title: Unused Share Conventions for Cancelled Waivers
content:
# Unused Share Conventions for Cancelled Waivers

*Refund actuarial note, Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda.*

When a holder cancels a Kessler GAP waiver and the refund is figured on the unused part of the term, the unused share depends on the length of the installment contract and on how long the waiver has been in force.

## The convention by term and age

| Contract term | Months in force at signing | Unused share |
|---|---|---|
| 72 months or longer | 12 or more | Whole calendar months from the signed request date to the expiration date, divided by the term months |
| 60 months or shorter | Fewer than 12 | Sum-of-the-digits share: unused whole months times (unused whole months plus one), divided by term months times (term months plus one) |
| Any other combination | — | Calendar-day share: calendar days from the signed request date to the expiration date, divided by calendar days from the sale date to the expiration date |

"Any other combination" includes a term of 61 to 71 months at any age, a term of 72 months or longer in force fewer than 12 months, and a term of 60 months or shorter in force 12 months or more.

## Counting months

- Months in force are whole calendar months from the sale date to the request date the holder signed.
- Unused whole months are whole calendar months from the signed request date to the expiration date.
- In both counts a whole calendar month counts each time the start date's day of the month is reached; an end date on an earlier day of the month does not complete the month, and there is no month-end adjustment.

The share chosen here is the share the refund is figured on: it multiplies the price amount the refund is figured from, and that product is rounded half up to the cent.

## Illustrations (hypothetical figures)

- **Sum of the digits.** A 48-month contract, waiver in force 8 months, 40 unused whole months, price 643.00: 40 times 41 is 1,640; 48 times 49 is 2,352; 643.00 times 1,640 divided by 2,352 is 448.3503..., rounded to 448.35.
- **Whole months.** An 84-month contract, waiver in force 24 months, 60 unused whole months, price 643.00: 643.00 times 60 divided by 84 is 459.2857..., rounded to 459.29.
- **Month count.** Sale on the 20th of a month; signing on the 19th of the month twelve months later: only 11 whole months are complete, so the waiver has been in force fewer than 12 months.
